newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Eight dissidents return to Cambodian royalist fold.
newsitem.headline: Eight dissidents return to Cambodian royalist fold.

text.p: Two lawmakers who briefly broke from the royalist FUNCINPEC party said on Monday that they had been encouraged to do so by co-premier Hun Sen in a bid to replace his coalition government rival Prince Norodom Ranariddh.

Relations between Second Prime Minister Hun Sen of the Cambodian People's Party (CPP) and First Prime Minister Ranariddh, head of FUNCINPEC, hit a new low on the weekend after Hun Sen claimed 12 FUNCINPEC MP's had split with the prince.
The move would have given the CPP and two smaller allies a majority in parliament for the first time, enabling them to pass legislation in the 120-seat house.

However, Royalist officials said on Sunday that eight of the dissident deputies had changed their minds, retracting support for Ung Phan, the FUNCINPEC Minister of State who had earlier challenged Ranariddh's leadership.
Two of the legislators said they had been pressured into supporting dissident royalist leaders Ung Phan, Toan Chhay and Duong Khem and one claimed they had been promised $10,000.
"Hun Sen was talking about the advantage and gain of the new form FUNCINPEC," said Min Saroeun, one of the returning deputies.
He quoted Hun Sen as saying they must try to get the support of enough MPs to control two-thirds or more of the house.
"He added that if we have the two-thirds, we can expel His Highness...(Ranariddh) from the prime ministership then give the premiership to Toan Chhay," Min Saroeun said.
FUNCINPEC has expelled five leaders of the breakaway wing, including Ung Phan, Toan Chhay and Duong Khem.
Ranariddh claimed on Sunday that Hun Sen was trying to destabilise FUNCINPEC and stage a "real coup d'etat."
Hun Sen on Saturday denied Ranariddh's charges that he engineered the rift but said his party had the right to agree with the prince's critics.
FUNCINPEC and CPP formed an uneasy coalition after U.N.-run polls in 1993. Tensions have heightened since a March 30 grenade attack that killed 19 people at a rally led by a FUNCINPEC ally.
